To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the chemical composition, antioxidant and antibacterial properties of depolymerised fucoidan were influenced by the extraction method of fucoidans.
the depolymerized water-extracted fucoidan showed a higher antioxidant and antibacterial activity.
the depolymerized Sargassum fucoidan showed higher antioxidant and antimicrobial activities than native Sargassum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the chemical composition and biological properties of depolymerised fucoidans obtained from S. tenerrimum.
the development and optimization of an extraction method of fucoidans from S. tenerrimum.
the development and characterization of fucoidans from brown macroalgae Sargassum sp. as potential natural antioxidants and antibacterial agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the fucoidan extracted by method two (DFM2, 1.09% yield) was more effective in antioxidant and antibacterial activity than fucoidan by method one (DFM1, 3.68% yield).
depolymerized Fucoidans are a promising candidate for further development as an antioxidant and antibacterial agent.
the fucoidan extraction method, the depolymerization process and the depolymerized degree of the fucan polysaccharide can affect its chemical composition, antioxidant and antibacterial activity.

depolymerized DFM2 from Sargassun tenerrimum could be a potential source of natural antioxidant and antimicrobial agent.
the depolymerization of fucoidans from S. tenerrimum by hydrothermal method is a promising technique for the production of fucoidants with higher antioxidant capacity and antimicrobials activity.
the DFM2 is a more promising fucoidan for its antioxidant and antibacterial potential than the DFM1.

depolymerized Sargassum fucoidan can be a promising candidate as an effective antibacterial agent and antioxidant with synergistic potential to decrease the prescribed dose of antibiotics in humans and animals.
the depolymerized Fucoidan from the S. tenerrimum can be used as a source for the development of novel natural products for the treatment of bacterial diseases.
